parsedVerdict.reasoning: AssignTaskUseCase fits the application layer: it coordinates a use case and leaves the actual rules to the domain. In execute(), it loads the task through the TaskRepository port and checks that the assignee exists through the UserRepository port. It then hands the assignment itself to the domain method task.assignTo(), saves the task through the port and returns it. It has no persistence code (no SQL, ORM or storage access), no transport logic (no HTTP request or response handling, no status codes) and no framework wiring. The typeof check on dto.assigneeId only guards input at the use-case boundary. The existence lookup is a cross-aggregate check that only the use case can do, because it needs both repositories. Neither one is a business invariant that belongs inside the domain entity. Throwing the domain's NotFoundError is a normal application-layer response when a lookup fails. No ADR text was provided.
